evidence.supports: Timeline confirms the proposed 8-month data-center moratorium was voted down 5-3 on April 6, 2026 and never took effect; the parish's subsequent June 1, 2026 ordinance is a standalone zoning ordinance, not a moratorium, and was introduced by the Parish President the same night the moratorium failed.

decisions.notes: REMOVE: the proposed 8-month data-center moratorium (File No. 2026-0114) was never adopted -- the Parish Council voted 5-3 against it on April 6, 2026, confirmed by both the parish's own record (via DataCenterSCP's timeline, sourced to Legistar/agenda materials) and contemporaneous Herald Guide news coverage. No moratorium instrument was ever in force in St. Charles Parish; the permanent data-center zoning ordinance adopted June 1, 2026 (Ordinance No. 26-6-3) is an independent, non-moratorium instrument introduced by the Parish President the same night the moratorium failed, not something that 'replaced' a pause that existed. The row's own current_status text already reaches this same conclusion ('No moratorium was ever in force'), so this row should not exist in the moratorium inventory at all; the underlying data-center-regulation story belongs, if anywhere, in a non-moratorium ordinance dataset, not here.
